## Project Design Document

SDR-Based Spectrum Monitoring System for FM Broadcast Screening and Compliance Assessment Support Continuous Monitoring of FM Broadcast Using HackRF One

Abstract. The document defines the end-to-end design of a low-cost, continuously operating SDR spectrum-sensing system for calibrated screening of FM broadcast services and technical support to compliance assessment. Its current required measurement outputs are per-channel calibrated received power and occupancy; duty cycle, noise-floor estimates, timing information, and related quality indicators are supporting observables. Carrier-frequency error, field strength, occupied bandwidth, adjacent-channel/out-ofband emission, and modulation-related quantities are not current required measurands unless later admitted through a controlled Requirements Baseline revision. The system integrates a HackRF One receiver with signal processing, measurement storage, visualization, and monitoring services. Project development follows the controlled engineering lifecycle defined in zz Workflow : project definition, requirements baselining, architecture and design, build and verification specification, prototype construction, and measured verification. Within that lifecycle, the prototype implementation sequence progresses through hardware characterization and calibration, sensor construction, PSD estimation, channel-power integration, adaptive occupancy detection, database logging, dashboard visualization, field validation, and multi-sensor deployment. The design emphasizes fixedgain calibrated sensing, quantitative detection and accuracy targets, reproducible validation, operational health monitoring, scalability, and mitigation of practical risks including overload, frequency drift, noise-floor errors, USB failures, and storage growth.

## 1 Introduction

## Lifecycle Role of This Document

This document is a consolidated engineering source document for the SDR prototype project. It contains project-definition context, requirement material, architecture and design decisions, implementation planning, and verification material used by the staged lifecycle defined in zz Workflow . It does not by itself replace or approve the controlled lifecycle artifacts. Where applicable, the authoritative Project Definition Baseline, Requirements Baseline, Architecture and Design Baseline, and Build and Verification Specification are the approved outputs of Ctx 00-Ctx 03, respectively. The numbered phases in this document describe the prototype implementation sequence and shall not be interpreted as substitutes for those lifecycle stages or readiness gates.

## Objective

Design, build, and field-validate a continuously operating spectrum-sensing sensor that monitors FM broadcast services and records per-channel received power and occupancy over time. The system must be low-cost, reproducible, and scalable from one sensor to a network of geographically distributed sensors reporting to a central database.

## Intended User

The intended user is the Agencia Nacional del Espectro (ANE) of Colombia, with operational use by personnel responsible for FM broadcast spectrum monitoring and technical support to compliance assessment.

## Operational Environment

The system is intended for continuous field deployment at FM broadcast monitoring sites in Colombia. The operational context includes an individual sensing node and subsequent extension to geographically distributed sensing nodes whose measurements are reported to a central repository. Monitoring is performed from received RF signals together with site-specific reference information, including applicable FM station assignments and calibration or reference measurements.

## Authoritative Technical and Regulatory Sources

The regulatory baseline is the Colombian spectrum and FM sound-broadcasting framework administered by the Agencia Nacional del Espectro (ANE). The authoritative regulatory sources are the Cuadro Nacional de Atribuci´ on de Bandas de Frecuencias (CNABF) and the Plan T´ ecnico Nacional de Radiodifusi´ on Sonora en Frecuencia Modulada (FM), established within Resoluci´ on ANE 105 de 2020 and the amendments in force on the approval date of the Ctx 00 Project Definition Baseline [ ? , ? , ? ]. Supporting technical sources include ITU-R BS.412, ITU-R SM.1268, and the official HackRF One documentation [ ? , ? , ? ]. IEC 62106 and IEEE 802.22 are supporting references only where their respective RDS or spectrum-sensing content is applicable.

## Scope

Authoritative Project Boundary - Current Scope. The project is limited to calibrated screening and technical support to compliance assessment. The system may provide calibrated measurements, monitoring records, quality indicators, uncertainty information, alerts, and other technical evidence to support review by the responsible regulatory personnel. It shall not independently establish formal regulatory compliance or non-compliance.

The complete Compliance-Grade / Conditional Compliance-Grade / MQR / MCC qualification framework is not required by the current project scope and shall not be incorporated as a system requirement. References to that framework in supporting technical sources shall be treated as design or assurance proposals outside the current Requirements Baseline unless a future documented stakeholder-approved scope change explicitly introduces formal compliance-grade measurement certification.

Calibration, traceability, uncertainty or quality characterization, acquisition integrity, measurement-validity checks, hardware limitations, and reviewable technical evidence remain applicable where source-supported and necessary for screening/support. This boundary does not establish any new operational facts or approve additional measurands.

Requirements-Admission Rule. Where supporting technical sources specify differing acquisition configurations, gain strategies, calibration procedures, hardware-capability claims, or additional measurands, those statements remain non-normative candidate evidence until explicitly admitted into the versioned Requirements Baseline. The current baseline shall define only the minimum controls necessary for FM channel occupancy and calibrated received-power screening and shall not inherit additional measurands, certification mechanisms, or implementation-specific controls solely because they appear in a supporting source.

- ❼ In scope: sensing and logging of FM broadcast occupancy and power; calibration against references; web visualization; multi-sensor aggregation.
- ❼ Out of scope (v1): demodulation/recording of audio content, transmitter geolocation, real-time regulatory enforcement actions.

## HackRF One Hardware Characterization

- Gain chain: The HackRF receiver path provides three digitally controlled gain stages: RF amplifier (AMP, 0/14 dB, fixed step), LNA (0-40 dB, 8 dB steps), and VGA (062 dB, 2 dB steps). The current calibrated-screening baseline uses declared fi xed gains. Individual gain settings and amplifier state shall be recorded with each acquisition, and clipping/integrity checks remain mandatory because a fixed gain value alone does not demonstrate valid acquisition. AGC is not part of the current baseline; it may be evaluated as an alternative only after separate validation and explicit admission into the Requirements Baseline. Recommended starting point for a moderate-signal urban/rooftop site: RF amp off (0 dB), LNA = 16 dB, VGA = 20 dB, then adjust per site using the overload checks in Section ?? .

The usable dynamic range and compression behavior shall be characterized empirically for the deployed gain configuration. No universal 60 dB dynamic-range requirement is imposed by the current baseline; adequacy is established by validation of the admitted occupancy and calibrated-power outputs under the intended signal environment.

- Frequency-reference characterization. The stock crystal is specified at roughly ± 20 ppm; at 100 MHz this is up to ± 2 kHz. For the current occupancy/power baseline, the frequency-reference state and any correction needed to preserve channelfrequency mapping shall be recorded per device. Carrier-frequency error is not a current required measurand. A TCXO, GPSDO, or equivalent disciplined reference becomes mandatory only if a later admitted measurement objective requires accuracy or stability that cannot be demonstrated with the baseline reference/verification method.

where v c = 1 when acquisition integrity and calibration validity are established for the scan (no receive overflow or dropped frame during the scan and an active, valid calibration record); P nf,c is the locally verified receiver noise level integrated over B c , in dBm at the receiver reference plane; and P req ,c is the declared minimum received power, at the same reference plane, that the sensor is required to detect on channel c . A channel is released as Free only when a signal at the required level would lie at least 10 dB above the verified noise level and above the active detection threshold. Its value is not defined by this document and remains an open item in the deferred-item register until admitted. The 10dB margin is selected within the 8 dB to 12 dB noise-margin range defined by ANE in the Manual de Gesti´ on Nacional del Espectro Radioel´ ectrico, T´ ıtulo V-Monitoreo del Espectro Radioel´ ectrico , Sec. 3.3.3.4.5, Configuraci´ on del umbral , for threshold configuration when the local noise level is known. That section also identifies FM/BC 88 MHz to 108 MHz as requiring band-specific background-noise treatment. ANE applies the margin to configure a detection threshold; this project applies the same margin as a sensitivity condition for releasing the Free state. The value is therefore a project selection supported by analogy with the ANE range, not a unique ANE-prescribed FM regulatory limit. It remains subject to FM-specific validation and controlled revision, and it does not replace the adaptive occupancydetection threshold γ .

- Upgrade path: cyclostationary detection FMbroadcasts carry a 19 kHz stereo pilot, producing strong spectral correlation peaks at cyclic frequencies α = ± 19 kHz. An SCD (spectral correlation density) test on candidate channels discriminates true FMemissions from noise, interference, or intermodulation products - implemented as a Phase 5/6 refinement to reduce false alarms near strong transmitters.
- Station identification (ground truth). Optional RDS demodulation (GNU Radio RDS blocks or the redsea CLI on narrowband-recorded IQ) extracts Program Identification (PI) codes and station names, giving positive station identification for validation in Phase 5.

## Validation Against Known References

- Test signals. ❼ T1: Recorded FM IQ replayed through a second SDR or RF playback path (known power, known frequency).
- ❼ T3: An independent reference receiver (RTL-SDR or spectrum analyzer) logging the same band. When T3 is used to verify PWR-001, its applicable amplitude calibration or characterization status, reference plane, and measurement uncertainty over the relevant frequencies and signal levels shall be documented and adequate to determine conformity with the ± 3 dB PWR-001 target. An uncharacterized receiver may support qualitative comparison but shall not serve as the reference for PWR-001 acceptance.
- ❼ T2: A locally receivable station with published parameters (frequency, ERP, site coordinates).
- Detector performance (OCC-001). The atomic OCC-001 validation observation is one annotated channel-scan pair, evaluated on the detector decision o c ; OCC-002 release behaviour is verified separately (Section ?? ). Use all annotated observations in the declared validation set; do not select or discard observations after detector outcomes are known.

Ground truth. A ground-truth occupied observation is a channel-scan pair carrying a T1 signal, or a station whose presence in the same period is confirmed by a qualified T3 observation; RDS identification may support but not replace that confirmation. A ground-truth vacant observation is a channel without an assignment in the site-specific station-assignment reference whose vacancy in the same period is confirmed by a qualified T3 observation. Absence from the assignment reference alone is not vacant ground truth.

Observation diversity. Consecutive scans of one channel are strongly correlated and shall not be treated as independent evidence. Each denominator shall: (i) contain at least 20 observations, the minimum count that resolves empirical rates in 5-percentage-point increments; (ii) draw on at least 10 distinct channels, with no single channel contributing more than 20% of the denominator; and (iii) separate observations of the same channel by at least a declared decorrelation interval τ dec . The values in (ii) and τ dec are proposed defaults pending admission into the Requirements Baseline and remain open items in the deferred-item register until admitted.

Acceptance statistic. Record TP , FN , FP , TN , the two denominator counts, the number of distinct channels per denominator, and the acquisition configuration used for evaluation, together with the two-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson interval for P d and P fa . OCC-001 is verified only when the point estimates satisfy P d ≥ 95% and P fa ≤ 5% under this procedure. The reported interval states how strongly the evidence bounds the target; at 20 observations, 19 detections give a lower bound of approximately 75%. Acceptance on a confidence bound rather than a point estimate would be a Requirements Baseline change. The released state s c of each annotated observation shall also be recorded, so that the Uncertain fraction per ground-truth class is reported.

- Power accuracy and channel-mapping integrity ❼ Channel mapping: compare the receiver frequency axis against a known reference; acceptance ± 5 kHz at 100 MHz (MAP-001). This is an acquisition-integrity criterion, not a current carrier-frequency measurand.
- ❼ Power: for each of at least 10 distinct channels, compute ∆ c = P c - P c, T3 against the qualified T3 reference, per Section ?? , and the expanded uncertainty U c of that comparison, with its coverage factor stated. PWR-001 is

satisfied only when every compared channel meets | ∆ c | ≤ 3 dB - U c . A channel with | ∆ c | &gt; 3 dB + U c fails PWR-001; a channel between these limits is inconclusive, and PWR-001 shall not be declared satisfied while any compared channel is inconclusive. The validation record shall identify the T3 reference and its applicable uncertainty. The ± 3 dB target is provisional and remains an open item in the deferred-item register until confirmed or revised in the Requirements Baseline.

## 5 Phase 3 - Measurement Database

## Technology Choice

InfluxDB 2.x is the default: native time-series storage, downsampling (retention policies), and direct Grafana integration. PostgreSQL/TimescaleDB is an acceptable alternative if relational sensor metadata must be colocated.

## Schema

Table 1.4: InfluxDB measurements (line-protocol tags/fields).

| Measurement   | Tags                            | Fields                                                                                                                                               |
|---------------|---------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| channel power | sensor id , freq mhz , location | power dbm , state (oc- cupied/free/uncertain), detector occupied (bool), noise floor dbm , gamma dbm , release margin db , gain lna , gain vga , , , |
| spectrum      | sensor id                       | amp state calibration id calibration state , validity flags psd (float array / blob sidecar) - optional waterfall history                            |
| health        | sensor id                       | rx overflows , frames dropped , records published , gain lna , gain vga , amp state , temp c , uptime s                                              |

Each calibrated channel power record shall retain the gain state used for that measurement and the calibration id of the applicable calibration record. That record shall resolve to the retained hardware/firmware applicability, receiver reference plane, and calibration validity information defined in Section ?? . Historical provenance shall therefore be reconstructable directly from persistent data without relying on temporal proximity to a separate health record. Each channel power record shall also retain the inputs of its released state ( detector occupied , gamma dbm , noise floor dbm , release margin db , and validity flags ), so that every released Free state can be re-checked against OCC002 from persistent data.

## Writer Service

A small Python daemon subscribes to the flowgraph's ZMQ PUB socket, computes perchannel metrics (Phase 2 math lives here, keeping the flowgraph thin), and batch-writes line protocol (batch size 100, flush 1 s). It also emits the health measurement every fullband scan and includes a reconnect/backoff on ZMQ or DB failure. The flowgraph shall stamp every published frame with a monotonically increasing sequence number. Because a ZMQ PUB socket discards messages without notice when a subscriber falls behind, the writer shall count sequence gaps as dropped frames. A full-band scan during which a receive overflow or a dropped frame occurs shall be marked invalid in validity flags ; its records are retained, are not used as verification evidence, and are released as Uncertain under OCC-002.

## 6 Phase 4 - Web Dashboard

## Grafana Panels

1. Occupancy heatmap (primary view): frequency × time, colour = channel power. This is the key broadcast-monitoring display.
2. Live spectrum trace : current PSD with channel markers and RDS-derived station labels.
3. Per-channel trends : 24 h power and duty cycle for selected stations.
4. Sensor table : online status, last scan age, noise-floor drift, receive-overflow and dropped-frame counts (multi-sensor ready).

## Alerting Rules

Alerts identify screening observations for personnel review; they shall not independently establish formal regulatory compliance or non-compliance.

- ❼ Channel silent: state = Free for T on-air hours on a station previously &gt; 90% duty cycle. Uncertain observations do not count toward silence.
- ❼ Unexpected-channel/anomalous occupancy: state = Occupied on monitored FM channels not present in the site-specific station-assignment reference.
- ❼ Sensor offline: no health point for 3 scan periods.

- ❼ Noise-floor drift: median noise floor shifts by &gt; 6 dB over 24 h (possible gain fault or interference).

## 7 Phase 5 - Field Validation

## Protocol

1. Select a site with a published FM station list (regulator data: frequency, ERP, transmitter coordinates).
2. Run the sensor continuously for 72 h. This run is an implementation-progress check; AVL-001 is verified only by the 30-day procedure in Section ?? .
3. Independently log the band with the reference receiver (T3) for at least 6 h overlapping the deployment.
4. Collect RDS identifications where possible for ground truth.

## Field-Validation Diagnostics

The following metrics are field-validation diagnostics. They are not acceptance criteria and are not part of the current Requirements Baseline; admitting any of them as an acceptance criterion requires a controlled Requirements Baseline revision. Their parameters, including the expected-station filter, shall be declared in the validation plan before the run.

- ❼ Detection rate: licensed stations detected / licensed stations expected at the site (the declared ERP-and-distance filter defines 'expected'). Reference value ≥ 90% of expected stations.
- ❼ Ranking consistency: Spearman's ρ between measured power ranking and predicted ranking ( P rad - FSPL), using the same declared radiated-power reference basis as the link-budget check. Reference value ρ ≥ 0 . 8.
- ❼ Stability: no unrecovered crashes; watchdog restart count logged; disk usage within budget (see Section ?? ).
- ❼ Error sources documented: multipath fading (slow power variation of ± 10 dB is normal for a fixed link over a day), intermodulation from strong FM signals (check phantom products at 2 f 1 - f 2 combinations), and front-end overload (add attenuation and re-run if observed).

## 8 Phase 6 - Multi-Sensor Deployment

## Architecture

Sensor nodes forward data to a central collector via MQTT (topic per sensor: spectrum/&lt;sensor id&gt;/c with the telegraf/agent or the writer publishing directly over TLS. The central instance runs InfluxDB and Grafana; dashboards aggregate all sensors using the sensor id tag.

## Time Synchronization

Cross-sensor comparison requires aligned timestamps:

- ❼ Minimum: NTP (Chrony), keeping nodes within tens of ms. ❼ For interference/correlation studies: GPS PPS or a shared GPSDO; note scan start times with sub-ms precision.

## Deployment

Each node ships as a docker-compose stack: flowgraph + writer + telegraf + (node exporter) . Per-node configuration file holds sensor ID, location, validated sample rate/scan plan, calibration table reference, and fixed gains - identical images across sites, configuration via environment. Storage budget: at 103 channels × 4 fields × 1 full-band scan/5 s, raw channel power volume is approximately 30 MB/day/sensor for 4-byte fields and 60 MB/day/sensor for 8-byte fields, before InfluxDB overhead. A 7-day raw retention with 1 h downsampling beyond 7 days keeps long-term storage negligible. Recalculate for site-specific channel count and scan rate.

## 9 Requirement Verification Procedures

- FRQ-001 (frequency range). Verified by (i) inspection: the declared capture plan places every channel allocation f c ± 100 kHz in the FRQ-001 range inside the validated usable span of at least one capture; and (ii) test: a T1 signal at the lowest and at the highest channel of the range produces valid channel power records with o c = 1 in every full-band scan of a declared test run.
- SCN-001 (scan period). The scan period is measured as the difference between consecutive full-band scan start timestamps t over a declared run in the deployment configuration. SCN-001 is satisfied when every measured interval is ≤ 10 s. An interval interrupted by a recorded watchdog restart is excluded from SCN-001 and counted against AVL-001. Acceptance on a percentile instead of every interval would be a Requirements Baseline change.
- OCC-002 (Free-state release). Verified by inspection of the stored records of the OCC001 validation set and of the 72 h field run. Every record with state = Free shall show detector occupied = false, valid acquisition and calibration flags, release margin db ≥ 10, and gamma dbm ≤ P req ,c . A single violating record fails OCC-002. The number of ground-truth-occupied observations released as Free shall be reported.
- AVL-001 (uptime). Over a continuous 30-day window, the sensor is available at time t when a valid full-band scan record exists within the preceding three declared scan periods, the same window used by the sensor-offline alert. AVL-001 is satisfied when the available time is at least 95% of the window. The 72 h field run does not verify AVL-001.
- SCL-001 (scalability). At least five sensors concurrently deliver channel power and health records to one central database over a declared verification period. SCL001 is satisfied when, for every sensor, the records are attributable by sensor id

and the central record count equals the sensor's records published count for the period.

## 10 Risk Register

Table 1.6: Top risks and mitigations.

| Risk                                                          | SeverityMitigation   | SeverityMitigation                                                                                                                                     |
|---------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Absolute power inaccuracy (HackRF uncalibrated)               | High                 | Per-device calibration table (Sec. ?? ); fixed gains; periodic re-check against a known station (T2).                                                  |
| Front-end overload near transmitters                          | High                 | Monitor for intermod products at 2 f 1 - f 2 ; reduce LNA/VGA; add external attenuator; AMP stays off by default.                                      |
| USB dropouts and sample loss on long runs                     | Medium               | Log receive overflows and dropped frames in health ; mark affected scans invalid; watch- dog (systemd Restart=always); alert on missing health points. |
| Frequency-reference drift affecting channel mapping (MAP-001) | Low                  | Characterize per-device offset/state; log drift trend in health ; use a disciplined reference only when a later admitted objective requires it.        |
| Noise-floor mis-estimation causing P fa violations            | Medium               | MAD-based adaptive threshold; cyclostationary confirmation (Phase 5/6).                                                                                |
| Database disk growth                                          | Low                  | Retention policies and downsampling (Sec. ?? ).                                                                                                        |

|       0 | Spec & calibration signed off | Occupancy/power outputs approved; amplitude calibration/verification and occupancy-threshold validation defined                                                                              |
|       1 | Sensor online                 | 60 s clean run, zero receive overflows and zero dropped frames, ZMQ streaming                                                                                                                |
|       2 | DSP validated                 | OCC-001, PWR-001, MAP-001 veri- fied on T1-T3; OCC-001 uses the de- clared channel-scan/SNR evaluation con- tract, diversity constraints, and recorded confusion-matrix counts               |
|       3 | Logging live                  | ≥ 1 h of queryable DB data                                                                                                                                                                   |
|       4 | Dashboard live                | Heatmap + alerts firing in Grafana                                                                                                                                                           |
|       5 | Field validated               | Field-validation diagnostics evaluated against their declared reference values; 72 h continuous run with no unrecovered failures. AVL-001 is verified by the 30-day procedure (Section ?? ). |
|       6 | Network live                  | ≥ 2 sensors aggregated centrally; SCL- 001 ( ≥ 5 sensors) verified by the proce- dure in Section ?? .                                                                                        |

- ❼ FFT frame: one N FFT -sample block.
- ❼ PSD update: averaged periodogram over M FFT frames.
- ❼ Capture: one contiguous IQ block at a single centre frequency.
- ❼ Full-band scan: one complete measurement across the FM band (one or more captures, depending on coverage).
- ❼ Scan period: time between consecutive full-band scans.
